results.reason: Issue 2 calculates the Section 3.2 deadline as August 16, 2026 and treats it as likely passed, inferring from the Schedule 3.12 'intends to deliver' note that no notice was delivered. It explains the agreement expires November 14, 2026, before the November 30, 2026 target closing. It also says the MIPA § 3.12(c) 'through November 2029' rep would be false, exposing Sellers to an indemnification claim.

Issue 1 identifies the 100% sale as a Change of Control requiring Velloran's prior written consent under § 14.2, with a termination right under § 14.3. It notes the consent is omitted from Schedule 3.6 and therefore from the § 7.1(d) closing condition. It recommends adding the consent and obtaining it before closing.

The response identifies that the Side Letter expands the Territory to six states (adding NY and VA) versus four for exclusivity, including the 18-month tail, and recommends narrowing the territory. However, it never explains that the expanded definition controls because of the § 19.4 order-of-precedence clause. Section 19.4 is cited only in the separate governing-law issue, not tied to the Territory definition.

Issue 6 identifies New York law and New York County forum in Side Letter § 6 versus Delaware law (§ 18.1) and Wilmington forum (§ 18.2). It explains the risk of threshold litigation and split treatment of related claims, and recommends aligning governing law and forum across the agreement stack.
States that the Initial Term ends November 14, 2026.
States the Target Closing Date is November 30, 2026.
States the Distribution Agreement Territory is four states: DE, MD, NJ, PA.
The memorandum is addressed to [Partner], and each issue has Documents and Sections, Why it matters, and Recommendation subsections.

The most critical issues (Velloran consent, renewal deadline) come first, followed by a priority table. It expressly says to 'Raise with Quillon's counsel promptly' and to confirm immediately with the client.
The response does not conclude that the agreement renewed or can still be timely renewed. It notes there is no automatic renewal and that the deadline likely passed.
The response explicitly states that Velloran's consent is absent from Schedule 3.6 and not a closing condition.
